sentences.text: This small sauropod measured 9 meters long and weighed just one tonne, featuring a slender build with a U-shaped lower jaw and slender, conical teeth.
It holds the unique distinction of being the first dinosaur named in a publication released entirely online.
Despite its classification as a sauropod, its tiny size of only one tonne makes it remarkably light for such a large-bodied group.
The holotype, consisting of a lower jaw fragment and twenty teeth, was discovered in the Mwakasyunguti area of the Karonga District in Malawi between 1987 and 1992.
Elizabeth Gomani formally described the type species Karongasaurus gittelmani in 2005.
Gomani classified the animal within the infraorder Sauropoda and assigned it to the unranked family Titanosauria.
Fossil evidence places this creature in the environment of the Aptian stage, spanning from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
